newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher after note auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher after note auction.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher after extending gains in light late afternoon trade.
Some traders said the U.S. Treasury's $12 billion five-year note auction produced favorable results, and helped buoy June T-bonds towards the high of 109-12/32 reached last Thursday and Friday.
"The question after the auction was if it was mostly the street bidding it up or if it was real money," one bond market analyst said.
A high yield of 6.616 percent was produced from the Dutch auction of five-year notes.
Traders, on average, were expecting a high yield of 6.22 to 6.23 percent.
He said the Dutch auction, in which prices are lowered gradually until a responsive bid is seen, may have skewed the results of the auction.
However, he added that "the Street doesn't seem to be overly weighed with paper."

Interest from dealers and funds was reported in the T-bond futures pit, with moderate-sized bids seen at the 109-05/32 to 109-07/32 area. Two U.S. dealers each bought about 1,000 June contracts. Later four firms bought a total of 2,000.
"Over the last couple of days, I would say funds bought about 25,000 contracts," one futures trader said, adding that some funds and banks were looking to extend duration.
They established long positions once the yield on the long cash bond fell to the seven percent level.
T-bonds were all the more attractive as the dollar appreciated against the yen, they said.

Some traders also said the continued turmoil in Germany over the government's plan to revalue gold was leading to flight-to-quality buying in bonds and Eurodollars as investors moved money out of German bunds.
Several market analysts noted the divergence between higher T-bond prices and lower U.S. stock prices.
"We've been hearing some talk of asset reallocation," one analyst said. "Funds and portfolio managers reassessed the situation after yields on bonds reached seven percent."

Revisions to first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product data will be released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Friday. GDP growth is forecast to be revised up to 6.0 percent, from 5.6 percent as originally reported. Some traders are looking for GDP to show a gain as high as 6.5 percent.
U.S. April new home sales, which will be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, are expected to slip to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 800,000 from 813,000 in March.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were up 19/32 at 109-10/32, September T-bonds were up 19/32 at 108-30/32, June 10-year T-notes were 07/32 higher at 107-00, and December Eurodollars were up 0.045 at 93.70. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
